strengths: The paper addresses a clear question with an identifiable audience in online learning: adapting to an unknown switching budget in adversarial bandits. The distinction between known and unknown budgets is well motivated.

The logarithmic grid of candidate budgets and the master/base regret decomposition provide a coherent construction. The discussion of how importance weighting affects variance offers useful methodological insight.

Explicit pseudocode and detailed intermediate derivations make the approach inspectable. The paper also acknowledges that optimal worst-case adaptation remains unresolved. Source: :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-xzkbvjs2/call-a93dfe7171224781835a1c7612d5ccca/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: Necessary: Theorem 2's headline guarantee is unsupported by the stated learning rate. Algorithm 2 sets η = sqrt(H/T), so Lemma 4 contributes a negative term −E[ρ_T]sqrt(T)/(40sqrt(H)log T). Equation (17) incorrectly introduces an additional sqrt(K). Even granting the preceding lemmas, maximizing the correctly substituted expression gives O-tilde(SK sqrt(T)), rather than O-tilde(S sqrt(KT)). Correct the algorithm and proof, or weaken the theorem and dependent comparisons. This polynomial discrepancy is the principal reason for leaning reject.

Necessary: Repair the clipping and estimator arguments. Equations (4) and (8) maximize the discrepancy between an arbitrary clipped distribution and a comparator vertex, then bound it by the cost of a particular smoothed comparator. For two arms and loss (0,1), the maximum discrepancy from the first-arm vertex is 1−β, not β. Selecting a specific smoothed comparator offers a plausible repair, but the displayed transitions are invalid. Lemma 2 also applies a pathwise OMD bound to the true losses although the update uses estimated losses; the expectation argument needs to be supplied correctly.

Necessary: State and enforce valid parameter ranges. Algorithm 1 requires αH ≤ 1 for its clipped simplex to be nonempty, but the chosen α violates this when T < KH^(3/2). The lower bound in Section 2.1 also cannot hold throughout the stated range because sqrt(SKT) can exceed T, whereas regret cannot. Provide appropriate restrictions or a bound saturated at T.

Necessary: Correct the implementation guidance in Remark 1. Its cumulative-loss formulas do not describe the adaptive, clipped OMD updates used in Algorithm 2. Mixing an unconstrained update with the uniform distribution is also generally different from the required Bregman projection. Supply valid update procedures or establish guarantees for the proposed implementation variant.

Optional: Give an interpretable example or problem class where ρ_T(h†) stays small enough to improve the adaptive bound. Its definition through inverse master-selection probabilities currently leaves the practical benefit difficult to assess. Experiments could illustrate this, but are not required for acceptance of a sound theoretical contribution.
